newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FISCHER TAKES AUSTRALIA'S RACIAL AGREEMENT OVERSEAS
Trade Minister Tim Fischer has confirmed the Federal Government has stepped up diplomatic efforts in a bid to limit damage from the race debate.
Mr Fischer says concedes he's received reports of Asian tourists and students cancelling visits to Australia.
Federal Parliament this week endorsed a bi-partisan motion on racial tolerance.
Mr Fischer, who leaves tomorrow for a trade mission visit to India, says he'll distribute copies of the bi-partisan motion on his trip, via Thailand and Singapore.
WOODCHIP LICENCES WELCOMED
The Federal Government's allocation of new export woodchip licences has been hailed as environmentally responsible.
Eleven companies around the country will export 19-million tonnes of woodchips from native forests over the next three years.
Five of them are in Tasmania ... and that state's Forest Protection Society says the allocation of new licences will bring certainty to the timber industry.
The Forest Industries Association of Tasmania also has welcomed the government's decision.
DEPARTMENT HEAD TAKES BLAME FOR WRIGHT FAMILY
The Head of the Department of Employment has told a Senate hearing that the Department accepts the responsibility for the creation of the fictitious Wright family.
The Wright family was constructed to highlight a point that millionaire families can claim Austudy and other welfare benefits.
It was used as an example by Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone at a Senate Committee meeting and she was subsequently forced to apologise to the Committee when it was found to be ficticious.
Department head Sandy Hollway has apologised to the Senate committee and the Minister who he says wasn't accurately informed on the status of the family.
AUSSIE WINE PRODUCERS TOLD TO STICK TO THEIR GUNS
Australian wine producers are being urged not to compromise the reputation of their product, by catering to the wine tastes of the Chinese.
Muswellbrook wine-maker Andrew Cruikshank says Australians wines would suffer if they're produced solely to suit the Chinese market, where sweet red wines are favored.
He says Australian exporters should go into the market with existing wines, and promote their distinct qualities.
ALARMING STATISTICS ON CHILDREN OF CRIMINALS
Children whose parents have come up against the long arm of the law are nearly 300 times more likely than other children to end up in gaol.
Those statistics will be presented today to a NSW parliamentary committee inquiring into the treatment of children whose parents are imprisoned.
The submission will be made by the Sydney based group Justice Action.
AUSTRALIAN COAT OF ARMS WANTED AT GOVERNMENT HOUSE
Liberal Senator Alan Eggleston has asked the Prime Minister to consider changing the coat of arms at Government House from the British to the Australian emblem.

Senator Eggleston says Government House is the official residence of the Australian head of state .. so it would seem inappropriate to have anything but the Commonwealth of Australia on the portico to the official entrance.
He says if US President Bill Clinton visits Government House next month, he'll pass through an entrance surmounted by the national coat of arms of a country other than the Commonwealth of Australia.
Senator Eggleston says everyone he's spoken to in Parliament agrees the Australian emblem should be used.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
